title_text: Association between coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance and ischemic stroke in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
description_text: Stroke is a devastating complication following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Coronary microcirculatory dysfunction (CMD) is implicated in adverse post-STEMI outcomes, but its relationship with subsequent stroke is unknown. We aimed to investigate the association of the coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (caIMR), a novel non-invasive tool for assessing CMD, for new-onset ischemic stroke in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI). This single-center, retrospective cohort study enrolled 602 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent successful pPCI between July 2020 and February 2025. The caIMR was calculated post-procedure using specialized software. The primary endpoint was new-onset ischemic stroke. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess the association between caIMR and stroke risk. Over a median follow-up of 29.3 months, 38 patients (6.3%) developed a new-onset ischemic stroke. In the multivariable Cox model, caIMR was independently associated with the risk of ischemic stroke (HR: 1.044, 95% CI: 1.022-1.065, P < 0.001), along with new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR: 9.113, 95% CI: 4.587-18.107, P < 0.001). A linear dose-response relationship was observed between caIMR levels and the risk of stroke (P for non-linearity = 0.975). Reclassification analysis showed that adding caIMR improved risk classification, with an IDI of 0.0307 (95% CI: 0.0031-0.0636; P = 0.030) and an NRI of 0.3887 (95% CI: 0.3156-0.4618; P < 0.001). Elevated caIMR is independently associated with an increased risk of long-term ischemic stroke in STEMI patients after pPCI. This easily accessible metric may serve as a valuable tool for future risk stratification in this patient population.

title_text: Can professional development effectively improve the in-service computer science teachers' teaching practice? A mixed methods study
description_text: Abstract This study investigates the effectiveness of professional development (PD) programs in enhancing the teaching practices of in-service computer science (CS) teachers in Pakistan. Two complementary studies were conducted: Study 1 employed a quantitative research, while Study 2 utilized a qualitative research. The findings of Study 1 revealed a significant positive relationship between PD programs and both teaching practices (TP) and self-efficacy (SE); however, no significant relationship was found between PD and job satisfaction (JS). Self-efficacy positively influenced both JS and TP, whereas no direct relationship was observed between JS and TP. Age emerged as a significant negative predictor of TP. Furthermore, SE was found to mediate the relationship between PD programs and TP, indicating that well-structured PD initiatives enhance CS teachers’ instructional techniques, confidence, and technological competence. These findings underscore the importance of designing PD programs that support student success in CS courses and strengthen teachers’ instructional efforts. Equipping CS teachers with appropriate tools and resources to create effective teaching learning environments is essential for achieving educational objectives. The results of Study 2 demonstrated that PD programs significantly improve CS teachers’ content knowledge, instructional strategies, and skill development. PD enhances teachers’ understanding of CS concepts and their ability to integrate these concepts into classroom instruction, thereby making learning more effective and engaging. The availability of CS resources and the use of effective instructional practices were identified as critical factors in improving teaching practices. In-school interdisciplinary collaboration, such as regular weekly and monthly meetings with school leadership, provides valuable opportunities to discuss instructional strategies and address teaching challenges. Collaboration beyond the school further supports teachers by enabling the sharing of experiences, refinement of teaching approaches, and exchange of ideas. PD programs for CS teachers should emphasize resource integration, student collaboration, and hands-on learning. Continuous monitoring of progress, constructive feedback, and recognition of achievements are vital for sustaining teacher motivation and ensuring ongoing improvement in instructional practices and practical skills.

title_text: Derivation of a risk model to predict urinary incontinence during pregnancy: a research article.
description_text: The onset of urinary incontinence (UI) during pregnancy is related to urinary incontinence persistence in the postpartum and later years. We aimed to design a prediction model of urinary incontinence that could be used at the beginning of pregnancy and included clinical and ultrasound variables. Design: Prospective cohort study. Obstetrics and Gynecology Service of Santa Caterina's Hospital (Girona, Spain) between 2018 and 2020. Women at 12-14 weeks' gestation were invited to participate by consecutive sampling and a follow-up visit was carried out at 32-35 pregnancy weeks. During the visits, we collected clinical data, measured 2D ultrasound variables, and administered the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ-SF). We built a multivariable model to predict urinary incontinence, assessed its calibration and discrimination (with the area under the ROC curve), and performed an internal validation. All the analyses were carried out using the R software (version 4.1). We recruited 174 nulliparous pregnant women during the study period and designed two models to predict urinary incontinence based on the significant variables in the univariate analysis: the urethral mobility and body mass index (BMI). The OR (95% CI) for the BMI category > 30 kg/m2 was 4.24 (1.48-12.30) in the first model (introital urethral mobility and BMI) and 3.31 (1.13-9.62) in the second model (transperineal urethral mobility and BMI). The area under the ROC curve was 0.725 for the first model and 0.687 for the second model. These models were used to create an online urinary incontinence prediction calculator. We built two multivariable models to predict, at the beginning of pregnancy, the individual risk of each pregnant woman to develop moderate/severe urinary incontinence in the third trimester. These models may provide a foundation for the future development of tailored primary prevention strategies.

description_text: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs), which detach from primary tumors and enter the peripheral blood, serve as biomarkers for monitoring a patient's status following cancer therapy. In this study, we developed a microfluidic platform integrating dielectrophoresis and image recognition for the capture and detection of CTCs from blood sample. Experimental parameters included applied electric field strengths ranging from 12.5 to 32.5 × 10 Results demonstrated that the optimal CTC separation efficiency of 78 ± 2% was achieved at an electric field of 25 × 10

title_text: M4DTrack: A DICOM-Based Imaging Informatics Workflow for User-Supervised 4DCT Lung Tumor Motion Reporting.
description_text: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) is routinely used in radiotherapy simulation to evaluate respiration-induced tumor motion, but the motion information is often reviewed visually rather than captured as structured, phase-resolved data. We developed and evaluated M4DTrack, a DICOM-based imaging-informatics workflow for user-supervised 4DCT lung tumor motion analysis and structured, exportable three-dimensional center-of-mass (CoM) motion reporting. M4DTrack imports phase-resolved DICOM CT images, groups images by respiratory phase, displays linked axial/coronal/sagittal views, supports crosshair-based tumor localization and HU inspection, and applies seed or linked 3D-box initialization with sequential phase-to-phase HU-volume propagation. An 8-case lower-lobe lung 4DCT dataset (80 respiratory phases) was analyzed. Directional amplitudes, 3D vector amplitude, maximum phase-wise displacement, and agreement with independent ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were quantified. HU-weighted CoM amplitudes were 2.44 ± 1.44 mm, 2.64 ± 1.37 mm, and 6.04 ± 2.48 mm in X, Y, and Z patient-coordinate directions, respectively. Mean 3D vector amplitude was 7.26 ± 2.50 mm, and mean maximum phase-wise 3D displacement was 6.20 ± 2.10 mm. Biases versus ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were 0.01, - 0.84, and 0.23 mm for X, Y, and Z, respectively, with a 3D vector amplitude bias of - 0.29 mm. M4DTrack provides a user-supervised imaging-informatics bridge between qualitative 4DCT cine review and structured quantitative motion documentation. The pilot results support feasibility for generating exportable, phase-resolved tumor-motion metrics while preserving user-supervised review of 4DCT artifacts, HU-capture uncertainty, adjacent anatomy, and differences between CoM-based and extent-based measurements.

title_text: Mast Cell Infiltration Helps Distinguish Fibrosing Alopecia in a Pattern Distribution From Androgenetic Alopecia in Scalp Biopsy.
description_text: Mast cells are key regulators of cutaneous inflammation and are known to accumulate in response to various immunological stimuli. Although their role in several dermatological conditions has been established, their specific contribution to different forms of alopecia-particularly scarring versus nonscarring types-remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to compare the degree of mast cell infiltration across three distinct types of alopecia: androgenetic alopecia (AGA), fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution (FAPD), and lichen planopilaris (LPP). A total of 56 patients diagnosed with AGA, FAPD, or LPP were enrolled. Scalp biopsies were obtained from all participants, and diagnoses were confirmed through histopathological examination. Mast cell distribution and infiltration density were quantified and analyzed using SPSS and Stata software. The study was conducted with full ethical approval. The majority of participants (91%) were female, with a mean age of 44.3 years. FAPD was the most prevalent diagnosis (42.9%). LPP demonstrated the highest degree of mast cell infiltration, while AGA exhibited the lowest (ANOVA, p < 0.001). Post hoc analysis revealed significant differences between AGA and FAPD (-17.7%, p = 0.001) and between AGA and LPP (-20.1%, p = 0.001). Although mast cell infiltration was higher in patients over 40 years of age, this difference did not reach statistical significance. No significant association was identified between mast cell infiltration and patient sex. Mast cell infiltration is significantly more pronounced in scarring alopecias (LPP and FAPD) compared to non-scarring AGA, suggesting a shared immunopathological mechanism underlying follicular destruction in scarring subtypes. These findings also raise important questions regarding the potential inflammatory contribution of mast cells to AGA pathogenesis.

title_text: Population pharmacokinetics of levetiracetam in term neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and therapeutic hypothermia: The LEVNEONAT-1 study.
description_text: This study aimed to describe the pharmacokinetics (PK) of levetiracetam (LEV) in term neonates treated for neonatal seizures secondary to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). Fifteen neonates were included and received a loading dose ranging from 30 to 60 mg/kg followed by eight maintenance doses corresponding to one-fourth of the loading dose every 8 h. Five blood PK samples were drawn for each neonate: three after the loading dose and two after the last maintenance dose. Data were analysed by a population approach using NONMEM software. The possible relationship between LEV Cmax and AUC from time 0 to 4 h after the loading dose (AUC LEV PK was described by a two-compartment model with allometric scaling based on body weight. Typical values (%IIV) for LEV CL, central and peripheral distribution volume (Vc and Vp) and distribution clearance (Q) were 4.27 (15%) L/h, 46.5 (14%) L, 6.10 L (98%) and 1.75 L/h, respectively. Creatinine clearance (CLcr) and natremia were found to be significant covariates for LEV clearance (CL), CL increasing with CLcr and natremia. No relationship was found between LEV Cmax or AUC A population PK model of LEV in term neonates with HIE was developed. The influence of natremia was highlighted for the first time and could reflect the relationship between the encephalopathy severity and LEV PK in this population.

title_text: Students as Experts-In-Training for Quality Assessment of Computer Science OERs
description_text: Open Educational Resources (OER) are teaching, learning, and research materials that are freely accessible and openly licensed, allowing users to use, adapt, and redistribute them with few or no restrictions. This article presents a quality evaluation experience over a set of OERs, a prior step to a clusterization process based on specific criteria. The evaluators have been students, from a teacher training master's program, that were instructed in concepts related to Open Learning, digital educational repositories, design and production processes for digital educational materials, and OER quality standards. The experiment consisted of evaluating the OERs stored in an online repository called Procomun, resources associated with the discipline of Computer Science. The resources have been created by both professionals and the students themselves, with the aim of comparing production quality levels and various specific criteria between them. For this purpose, two types of evaluations were carried out. First, the quality of the repository’s semantic tagging, based on the Learning Object Metadata (LOM) standard, was assessed using the Metadata Quality Assessment Model. Second, the UNE 71362 standard was applied to a selected collection of OERs obtaining a set of spider diagrams. Finally, to evaluate the value of the quality assessment itself, two types of processes were carried out: students acted as evaluators of the resources they had produced themselves (as a self-assessment task), and peer assessment was also carried out by other students. The article describes the entire experience, the evaluation process, the quality framework and the results obtained in the experimentation.

title_text: The Structure of Research Careers in Computer Science: A Multidimensional Analysis of Productivity, Persistence, and Collaboration
description_text: Abstract Understanding how scientific careers evolve is essential for research evaluation and science policy. This study presents a large-scale longitudinal analysis of computer science researchers using publication records from DBLP covering the period 1936–2025. Based on a dataset comprising approximately 7.9 million publications and nearly 4 million authors, we investigate multiple dimensions of research careers, including productivity, career dynamics, authorship roles, and collaboration patterns. The results reveal that the strong increase in publications per researcher observed over time is largely explained by the expansion of collaboration rather than by growth in individual productivity. When productivity is adjusted using fractional authorship and page-based measures, long-term trends remain stable or even slightly decline. Career trajectories exhibit a characteristic life-cycle pattern, with productivity increasing during the first two decades of activity, reaching a peak, and subsequently declining. However, these aggregate patterns are strongly affected by survival effects: almost half of the researchers publish only a single paper, and substantial attrition occurs during the first years of academic activity. We further show that research roles evolve systematically throughout careers. Early-career researchers are more likely to occupy first-author positions, whereas senior researchers increasingly appear as last authors. At the same time, collaboration networks expand steadily while maintaining a stable core of recurring collaborators. Based on these findings, we propose a set of conceptual career archetypes that capture the heterogeneity of participation in computer science research. Overall, the results highlight the limitations of single bibliometric indicators and support multidimensional approaches to research evaluation.

title_text: Trust, Traits, and Turning Points: Decoding Operator Responses to Real-World ADAS Malfunctions.
description_text: OCCUPATIONAL APPLICATIONThis study found that high emotional trust in Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) showed a non-significant tendency toward slower manual intervention during malfunctions, and that an operator's personality was related to specific information needs. For practitioners, this indicates a critical safety gap where affective comfort, feeling "too safe" reduces readiness. To mitigate these risks, organizations should prioritize hands-on, simulated malfunction training. By exposing operators to controlled scenarios such as "phantom braking" events, practitioners can help them experience system limitations firsthand, rebuilding the protective skepticism and preparedness that sustained automation use tends to erode. Because occupational driving spans a range of operational models, safety protocols should be tailored accordingly. In managed fleets, organizations have an opportunity to implement personality-aligned Human-Machine Interface (HMI) configurations that address the specific cognitive and informational needs of individual drivers. For "Bring Your Own Device" (BYOD) gig platforms, where organizations cannot modify the vehicle's native systems, broader software-based interventions are more practical, for example, in-app geofenced warnings that alert drivers as they approach known ADAS limitation zones. Together, these targeted, context-sensitive interventions help recalibrate trust and prevent overreliance, supporting rapid recovery and sustained situational awareness across the diverse occupational contexts in which ADAS is now used.

title_text: Valorization of sorghum stalk lignocellulose for xylooligosaccharide production: process optimization and chromatographic characterization.
description_text: Sorghum stalk (Sorghum bicolor) represents an abundant and underutilized lignocellulosic biomass with significant potential for the generation of value-added bioproducts within biorefinery systems. In the present study, sorghum stalk (SS) biomass was valorized for the production of xylooligosaccharides (XOS) through alkaline extraction of xylan, followed by enzymatic hydrolysis. SS was treated with alkali to extract high-purity xylan, where increasing NaOH concentrations significantly (p < 0.05) enhanced xylan recovery. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy indicated that xylan extracted using 3 M NaOH contained minimal lignin and represented a higher recovery (87.17 ± 0.32%). Enzymatic hydrolysis of extracted xylan, as optimized using Design-Expert software, resulted in maximum XOS production at pH 5.5, 45.45 °C, 24 h incubation, and an enzyme dose of 20 IU per 200 mg xylan. Analytical characterization revealed that the hydrolysates predominantly contained XOS with a degree of polymerization ranging from 2 to 6, primarily composed of xylohexaose. The produced XOS exhibited promising prebiotic potential for Lactobacillus salivarius, as evidenced by a higher prebiotic index (1.74 ± 0.04) than galacto-oligosaccharides (1.12 ± 0.03) and inulin (1.27 ± 0.08), together with the highest prebiotic activity score (13.42 ± 0.27) under the experimental conditions evaluated. The XOS also demonstrated concentration-dependent gradual increase in DPPH scavenging capacity, ranging from 23.02% at 0.125 mg/mL to 75.83% at 4 mg/mL. Furthermore, the XOS showed a higher resistance to simulated gastric conditions (pH 1-5), with less than 6% hydrolysis after 6 h. Overall, the findings highlight SS as a promising lignocellulosic biomass for the sustainable production of XOS and support their potential as high-value bioproducts derived from agricultural residues.

title_text: Voice and speech as digital biomarkers of mental health: a scoping review of clinical interpretability, data collection and translational readiness.
description_text: Voice and speech encode acoustic, linguistic, and interactional information associated with mental health. Translating these signals into clinically meaningful digital biomarkers depends not only on predictive performance but on how speech is elicited, how the target state is defined, whether findings generalize beyond the original dataset, and whether features can be measured reliably in real-world settings. To map voice, speech, language, and communication biomarkers studied across mental health outcomes and to examine three dimensions of translational readiness: clinical interpretability, evidentiary validity, and deployability. This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, PsycINFO, and Scopus were searched through June 18, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data. Biomarkers were classified as directly clinically interpretable, software-derived with a perceptual correlate, or technical-only. Of 1,524 records identified, 68 studies were included. Depression was examined in 56 studies (82%), followed by anxiety ( Voice-based mental health research identifies numerous candidate biomarkers, but translational readiness remains limited. Most evidence derives from depression and controlled speech tasks, and interpretability does not imply validity or deployability. Existing studies do not establish that candidate biomarkers remain valid in spontaneous, multispeaker, passive, or ambient clinical settings. Future work should prioritize validated outcome labels, longitudinal naturalistic capture, external validation, diverse populations, and explicit evaluation of interpretable and technical features across recording contexts.

title_text: Why students with an apparent aptitude for computer science don't choose to major in computer science
description_text: The statistics show that the number of Computer Science majors is dropping across the United States. Possible reasons include a reduced number of jobs in the field, an incorrect perception of what Computer Scientists do, and the students' disinterest due to a lack of familiarity with the subject. The reasons may be different for males and females. This paper reports on a study in which 836 high school calculus and pre-calculus students were surveyed to try to determine why students with an apparent aptitude for CS did not pursue a major in Computer Science. The results supported some of the hypotheses for declining enrollment, and rejected others. The top reasons for rejecting the major were the same for both genders, but the reasons for choosing the major differed.
